title: Salesforce Constant Contact Integration Without Code
summary: Salesforce Constant Contact integration syncs contacts when records update. You'll configure this workflow using Activepieces or similar automation tools.
body_markdown:
## Building the Salesforce Constant Contact sync


Build the sync in four stages. Each leaves something that works: connected accounts, a trigger with real data, a mapped action, then a published flow you've checked in both apps.


You can also skip the clicking for the standard steps.


Describe the job to a platform's built-in chat, such as "add each new Salesforce lead to my Constant Contact list", and it publishes a live flow in your account: the same trigger, the same "Create or Update Contact" action and the same field mappings you would have assembled by hand, each visible in the editor.


Every run of it leaves a trace showing what each step received and what it sent on.


That flow sits under the same RBAC, audit logs and run traces as one built by hand, and companies such as MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run automation platforms of this kind in production.


Keep the six-step sequence below beside you as you build. It shows the order the flow runs in, from connecting both accounts to publishing, so you can see where each stage leaves something to check.


### Connecting Salesforce and Constant Contact accounts


Sign in to Salesforce, the system that holds your leads, and to Constant Contact, where the email lists live. Authorize each connection with an account that can actually see the leads and edit the target list.


A connection made with a read-only login looks fine until the action step fails.


### Stage 2: add the Salesforce trigger and load sample data


Add the **New Lead** trigger and select your Salesforce connection. Then run the trigger's test so it pulls a real lead record from your org.


Pick a lead whose email, first name and last name are all filled in, because a sparse record gives you a mapping step with nothing to choose from.


In stage 3, add the **Create or Update Contact** action and select your Constant Contact connection. Map four fields from the trigger's sample data:


- Email
- First name
- Last name
- List


Choose the list by name from the dropdown rather than pasting an identifier. Map email first, since it's what Constant Contact uses to recognize a contact it already has.


In stage 4, run the action's test with the sample lead, then publish. Open the run trace and confirm each step shows the values you expect.


To verify, look in both apps. In Salesforce, open the lead you used and confirm the email and name match what the trace shows. In Constant Contact, search for that email and confirm one contact exists, with the right name, on the right list.


If the contact appears twice or lands on the wrong list, the mapping is the culprit, not the trigger. Fix it there and republish.
